clue.text: Enthusiastic male team heading off

indicators.note: with its heading taken off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a party is a team of people; lose its first letter

explanation.surface: A keen men's side, setting off for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Team is read as party, a group working together, which then drops its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearty welcome or appetite is a warm, vigorous and wholehearted one.

clue.text: I agree to try and try

parts.note: a judge will hear, or try, a case

explanation.surface: Someone nodding along while being urged to keep trying.
explanation.walkthrough: Try is used in its legal sense, as a judge tries a case, twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry is a parliamentary interjection voicing approval of what a speaker has said.

clue.text: Seaman's popular article is good for a drink

parts.note: AB, able seaman, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A sailor's favourite story recommends a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green anise-flavoured spirit, a liquor once famous in Parisian cafes.

clue.text: Brusque, in sister's estimation

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: spans the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: In my sister's opinion, someone is rather curt.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe speech that is short, abrupt and lacking in warmth.

clue.text: A British opera, length unusual

explanation.surface: A British opera that runs unusually long.
explanation.walkthrough: Norma is the Bellini opera, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abnormal departs from what is typical, so it is out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Getting on? Put up pension

parts.note: getting on a train or plane
to house someone is to put them up

explanation.surface: An ageing person asks whether to take their retirement pension.
explanation.walkthrough: Pension looks like retirement money, but it is the French-style lodging house; getting on looks like ageing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pension in continental usage is a small guesthouse offering lodging and meals.

clue.text: Collection made by Conservative supporting bid

indicators.note: in a down entry, the supporting part sits underneath the other

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A fundraising drive organised by a Tory backing an offer.
explanation.definitionFit: The offertory is the collection of money taken from the congregation during a church service.

clue.text: Large number blowing top after start of match

indicators.note: blowing its top means losing the first letter
places the remaining letters behind the opening piece
'start of' keeps only the first letter of 'match'

explanation.surface: A big crowd loses its temper after kick-off.
explanation.walkthrough: Number is EIGHTY, which blows its top letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mighty can mean huge or massive in scale, as in a mighty oak.

clue.text: Agree to take off and attack

parts.note: to let is to allow or agree to
as a bird or plane does

explanation.surface: Permission is given for the planes to depart and strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To let fly is an idiom for launching a verbal or physical assault on someone.

clue.text: Derby winner in USA, possibly blazing a trail

indicators.note: possibly signals an alternative form, and blazing suggests the letters set alight and scattered

explanation.surface: A racehorse from the Derby, perhaps trailblazing in America.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is the famous English flat race at Epsom; Australia won it in 2014.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia was the racehorse that won the Epsom Derby in 2014, an example of the category.

clue.text: Outstrip lad with vast engine, surprisingly

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is an unexpected arrangement

explanation.surface: A boy with a huge motor races past everyone, to general astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave others standing is an idiom for surpassing them easily.

clue.text: Good hospital entering appropriate contest

indicators.note: the pair goes into the middle of the other word

explanation.surface: A worthy medical centre joins a suitable competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight is a contest or bout between opponents, as in boxing.

clue.text: Fairy tale, a legend, enthrals when broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast once meant scattered widely, like seed sown by hand

explanation.surface: A storybook legend captivates listeners when read out on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grimm brothers' story of two children and a witch's gingerbread house is a classic fairy tale.

clue.text: A grant secured by the gymnast, perhaps

indicators.note: something secured is held inside what secures it

parts.note: to grant is to let or allow

explanation.surface: A sports grant has been obtained by the gymnast.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast is one example of a sportsperson, hence the perhaps.

clue.text: Elaborate stitch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to embellish a story with invented detail
second meaning: to decorate cloth with needlework

explanation.walkthrough: Elaborate looks like an adjective but is the verb, to add detail.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both decorating fabric with thread and adding colourful detail to an account.

clue.text: One dubious name for a gaseous element

indicators.note: something dubious is unreliable and not in its true form

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a questionable label for a gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a noble gas, the chemical element used in glowing advertising signs.

clue.text: Watchful living at resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort the letters again

explanation.surface: An alert holidaymaker staying at a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Resort looks like a holiday town; split it as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigilant describes someone keeping careful watch for danger or trouble.

clue.text: Enjoying great health? Yes

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an expression of agreement

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as question and answer; each half is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase can describe someone in fine health or serve as a reluctant agreement, like all right then.

clue.text: Touch brass instrument in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards

explanation.surface: A band player handling a horn while withdrawing.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that abut share a boundary, so they touch at the edge.

clue.text: Erratic heir, way out

indicators.note: out as in out of order, no longer in place

explanation.surface: An unpredictable heir who is very far gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Going haywire means behaving wildly or malfunctioning, out of control.

clue.text: Kudos involved first to unravel puzzle

indicators.note: involved means twisted and complicated
'first to' keeps only the first letter of 'unravel'

explanation.surface: There is prestige in being the first to crack a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudoku is the number-placing logic puzzle on a nine-by-nine grid.

clue.text: Fish dead? Moved on ice

explanation.surface: A fish is found dead and slid across a frozen pond.
explanation.definitionFit: To skate is to glide over ice on blades; the past tense matches moved.

clue.text: Unpredictable type, any one of the last three characters?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person nobody can read

definitions.text: any one of the last three characters?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: x, y or z in algebra

explanation.walkthrough: The last three characters are the alphabet's final letters, which algebra uses for variables.
explanation.definitionFit: In algebra x, y and z stand for values not yet found; figuratively the phrase means an unpredictable person.

clue.text: Square up holding end of lager bottle

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top
the outer word holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: to square a score is to even it

indicators.note: 'end of' keeps only the last letter of 'lager'

explanation.surface: Settling the bill while clutching the last of a beer bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for courage, and has nothing to do with the lager.
explanation.definitionFit: Having nerve means having courage or daring, which is what bottle means in British slang.

clue.text: "Chose" — past tense shown in dictionary

indicators.note: displayed within the other, so placed inside it

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry gives a verb's past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to choose, so the past tense matches chose.

clue.text: Make drunk supply a beer in it

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, meaning flexibly, so the letters bend into a new shape

explanation.surface: To get someone tipsy, provide them with an ale.
explanation.walkthrough: Supply looks like the verb provide, but is the adverb meaning in a supple way.
explanation.definitionFit: To inebriate is to intoxicate someone with alcohol.

clue.text: Like a minor in short dungarees, playing

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter goes
playing around with the letters rearranges them

parts.note: the overalls, with the final letter dropped

explanation.surface: A child in little overalls, playing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone under age is below the legal adult threshold, as a minor is.

clue.text: Vegetable in season, one pound

explanation.surface: Buying vegetables in season for a pound each.
explanation.definitionFit: The lentil is a legume, the edible seed of a pulse plant, loosely called a vegetable.
